Zillow Desk · Latent capital · as of 2026-09-30 (EDT)

The short version

Own Z for five to ten years as a housing marketplace with data and network effects — not a banner shop waiting for ChatGPT to erase the front door. What would change that view first is a sustained multi-quarter drop in monthly audience or the audience share the company itself quotes. A second warning would be Google or ChatGPT taking a meaningful and rising slice of housing search. That share series is still blank.

This page is the income, margins, shares, mix, traffic, and trailing-multiple scoreboard. History runs from 2015 where each print exists, including operating income beside adjusted EBITDA, diluted share count, EPS, operating income per share, and adjusted EBITDA per share. Fourth-quarter 2023 diluted shares are now on the series, so those per-share lines are on the chart for that quarter too.

Preferred attachment, For Sale take intensity, and relative revenue-per-connection uplift live on the unit-economics page. The AI and data-access question, and the management-quality read, live on their own pages. Links are at the end.

Risks

  1. Audience. A sustained multi-quarter drop in visits, average monthly unique users, or the issuer-quoted audience share would change the view before a single soft quarter would.
  2. Search shift. A language model or Google taking a rising slice of housing search is the other tripwire. The share itself is still blank, so the page does not invent it.
  3. Earnings quality. GAAP operating income is still near a loss. Trailing PE sits on thin net income, so the multiple is an honesty check beside adjusted EBITDA, not a clean cash-earnings multiple.
  4. Mix reading. The 2021 revenue spike is the Homes / iBuying company total. Residential plus Mortgages before fourth-quarter 2024 is not the printed For Sale line.

How it makes money

Zillow Group runs consumer brands — Zillow, Trulia, StreetEasy, HotPads — that pull demand for homes and apartments. Revenue shows up in three engines:

  1. Residential — Premier Agent and Preferred-style connection advertising, plus related for-sale marketplace products.
  2. Mortgages — including Zillow Home Loans purchase origination.
  3. Rentals — multifamily and rental marketplace revenue.

From fourth-quarter 2024 on, the company prints a For Sale subtotal (Residential plus Mortgages) that this page treats as fact. Rentals stands alone. Earlier modern quarters on the For Sale chart are Residential plus Mortgages, marked derived. Homes-era labels are not For Sale.

Resid, Mort, and Rentals as themselves — not a pre-2023 relabel.

For Sale runs from early 2023, marked derived through third-quarter 2024 and printed from fourth-quarter 2024. Rentals is the second locomotive on the same front door.

In second-quarter 2026 the company printed $772M total revenue, $549M For Sale, $209M Rentals, operating income −$10M (margin −1.3%), adjusted EBITDA $176M (margin 22.8%), GAAP loss −$4M / diluted EPS −$0.02, diluted weighted-average shares 227.9M, and adjusted EBITDA per share about $0.77. Cash was $572M. Survival is not the open question. Mix quality and take-rate are — and those sit on the unit-economics page.

Four series side by side from the mid-2010s where each print exists. The 2021 scale spike is the Homes / iBuying company total — not marketplace-only — so the era is labeled on the chart. Adjusted EBITDA prints the filings carried are on the series. Fourth-quarter operating income without a quarterly line is the year minus the first three quarters, marked derived.

Same history, in percent. GAAP operating margin is still near flat to negative while adjusted EBITDA margin holds in the low-to-mid 20s on recent marketplace quarters.

Share count through the Class C era and the recent buyback path. Early-2015 prints are the smaller pre-Class-C base, labeled on the chart. Fourth-quarter 2023 is 232.972 million diluted weighted-average shares. The latest print is 227.9 million in second-quarter 2026.

EPS is the printed figure when the filing has one. Otherwise it is net income over diluted shares, marked derived. Operating income per share and adjusted EBITDA per share use that same share base and are marked derived. Recent tape: EPS −$0.02, operating income per share −$0.04, adjusted EBITDA per share about $0.77. Fourth-quarter 2023, on the filled share count: EPS about −$0.31, operating income per share about −$0.45, adjusted EBITDA per share about $0.30.

Audience — soft, not collapsing

Q2’26 visits 2,529M / AMUU 239 versus Q2’25 2,590M / 243 — soft year-over-year, not a sustained collapse. Fourth-quarter prints are on the series: Q4’23 2,200 / 194, Q4’24 2,100 / 204, Q4’25 2,100 / 221.

Using Comscore figures the company itself quotes, Zillow Group held about 70% of the real-estate audience in both first- and second-quarter 2026. That is the sharper front-door print than raw AMUU alone.
